page: Microsoft Azure D64s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with Geekbench multi-core performance and static web serving throughput reaching the top 10% tier. Passmark database operations also rank in the top 10% tier, while Redis SET operations and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall within the top 25%. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth remains consistently strong across both cached small-block and uncached large-block read/write operations.

In terms of resource tradeoffs, the D64s_v6 does not include local storage, requiring reliance on external Premium Storage for data persistence. It also lacks complimentary public IPv4 addresses and dedicated GPU hardware. However, the high density of dedicated Intel Xeon cores combined with AMX instruction support provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require matrix math or vector calculations without the expense of dedicated GPU accelerators.

This server is suited for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, including database operations, high-throughput static web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference. The presence of AMX instructions makes it capable of handling prompt processing and text generation for 135M and 7B parameter models efficiently, though performance drops to average levels when executing text generation on larger 70B models.
